bug_semantics: A user who can configure CRM workflows/webhooks can supply an attacker-chosen destination URL. The application stores that URL and, when the workflow fires, sends an HTTP request from the CRM server without first constraining the scheme or rejecting loopback, private, link-local, reserved, or cloud-metadata destinations. This lets the user reach otherwise inaccessible internal services and infer or receive their responses. In the advisory's current route, POST /admin/settings/webhooks/create accepts end_point and the workflow dispatcher passes it to Guzzle.
flaw_origin: The underlying SSRF mechanism first became executable in ea3f9d66dbea8f56a5edbf3ab09323ae12c6e52e: packages/Webkul/Workflow/src/Helpers/Entity/Lead.php began passing the workflow-controlled action['hook']['url'] directly to Http::withHeaders(...)->post(...) without destination validation. The direct parent already had the webhook URL form but no outbound webhook request sink, so ea3f9d66dbea8f56a5edbf3ab09323ae12c6e52e is the smallest commit that completed the flaw. Later commits extended the same behavior to more entities, renamed Workflow to Automation, and centralized dispatch. In particular, 9bebb377ed610c10658092de580f2614aa6793db created the /settings/webhooks/create storage path with end_point validated only as required|string|max:255, and dec043c2d10241d2ea5051019595e9633b251b51 connected stored endpoints to a new unguarded Guzzle WebhookService; those are feature evolution/refactoring of the already-existing unvalidated webhook-request mechanism, not the original BIC.

reasoning: Commit-minimality reconciliation 2026-08-29: introducer corrected to dec043c2d10241d2ea5051019595e9633b251b51 after first-write/ancestry re-verification (see evidence tail). introducer_parent corrected to 245c4b1ba1317d6043cad315d431aa58c63e1264 (same recheck). BIC correction 2026-08-29: introducer_sha ea3f9d66dbea8f56a5edbf3ab09323ae12c6e52e -> dec043c2d10241d2ea5051019595e9633b251b51 after line-level first-write re-verification (see evidence tail). The vulnerability is the missing trust-boundary check between a user-configurable webhook URL and a server-side HTTP client. The 2022 workflow UI already collected hook[url], but direct parent 4406b1d6df95f8ba8b10a6da3808015eec3050ae did not dispatch it. BIC ea3f9d66dbea8f56a5edbf3ab09323ae12c6e52e added the first executable sink by sending that value through Laravel's HTTP client, so it is the smallest causal introducer. Later commits broadened the entity support and replaced inline workflow configuration with stored webhooks; 9bebb377ed610c10658092de580f2614aa6793db created the advisory's /settings/webhooks/create input and dec043c2d10241d2ea5051019595e9633b251b51 centralized the same unvalidated dispatch in Guzzle. Treating either later change as the BIC would incorrectly select a feature migration/refactor over the first flawed mechanism. Tags prove the flaw entered releases at v1.3.0, remained in v2.2.0 and the later v2.2.1-v2.2.4 tags, and was first released with the upstream fix in v2.2.5. The fix PR merge is 556dda0471880fc931da6f4d38ddbc949a458eec; its direct sink-side fix is 7f6b82de87ed64ba4ab5edc1b186006689a6ae92. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker, so under the required BIC-only rule the causal verdict is NOT_AI; AI signals on later refactors or fixes are irrelevant.
